speaker: Doctor
text: Please describe the duration of these unresponsiveness episodes and whether you or anyone else observed rhythmic jerking movements. Also, have you noticed any loss of bladder control or tongue biting during these events?

speaker: Patient
text: 7-year-old boy. The patient has been experiencing recurrent episodes lasting 3–4 minutes each of facial grimacing and staring over the past month. During these episodes, he is nonresponsive and does not recall them afterward. He reports a muddy taste in his mouth before the onset of these episodes. His brother witnessed him waking up, staring, and making hand gestures during one episode. The patient felt lethargic and confused afterwards.

speaker: Doctor
text: DIAGNOSIS READY: Absence Status Epilepticus (likely evolving from typical absence seizures). The prolonged duration of 3–4 minutes, post-ictal confusion, and specific aura (muddy taste) suggest a continuous or frequent cluster of absence seizures rather than isolated events. I recommend requesting an EEG to confirm the diagnosis and an MRI to rule out structural abnormalities.
